forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: New Forest Cabinet told of £1.25m budget gap in 2027/28, rising to £3.48m by 2030/31
news_drafts.lead:
New Forest District Council expects to be £1.25m short of the money it needs to balance its day-to-day budget in 2027/28, about 5% of its £26.63m budget, according to a medium-term financial plan (MTFP) put to its Cabinet on 7 October. The gap grows to a cumulative £2.443m in 2028/29, 9% of budget, and £3.484m by 2030/31.

The council's consultation document says the gap is mainly due to changes in government funding for local councils. The council holds a £1.199m Budget Equalisation Reserve, money set aside to protect against unforeseen pressures. The report says the reserve "is insufficient to mitigate the current scale of the budget gap" and can only be used once. It adds that the reserve should be regarded only as a very short-term solution. The council must set a fully balanced budget, and the report says that will need sustainable savings and income growth.

The council's separate housing revenue account, the ring-fenced account for its own housing stock, paid for by rents, is forecast to be in surplus by £406,000 in 2027/28. That falls to £310,000 in 2028/29 and £40,000 in 2029/30, then becomes a £190,000 deficit in 2030/31. The paper attributes this to pay and price inflation outpacing income growth, even assuming rent convergence goes ahead. The account holds £9.718m in reserves, including a £1m working balance. The paper says these could cover gaps only as a short-term measure, since they can be used once and would reduce funds for future capital programmes.

findings.paper_title: MTFP - Scene Setting - General Fund report and Appendices 1-5
findings.headline: MTFP assumes maximum allowable Council Tax increases without referendum (2.99% annually) projected to generate £1.995 million cumulative additional income by 2030/31
findings.detail: Council plans to maximize government's allowable Council Tax increase threshold without triggering referendum, assumed at 2.99% annually throughout the MTFP period. This strategy is expected to generate annual additional income of £473.5k in 2027/28 rising to £524.6k by 2030/31, totaling £1.995m cumulative additional income. Council is explicitly adopting this as part of strategy to 'make the most of the local tax raising flexibilities as set out by Central Government'.
findings.matters: Shows council maximizing available tax levers; continued reliance on government maintaining 2.99% referendum threshold; cumulative £2m of identified income contributes meaningfully to bridging the deficit; pattern demonstrates all councils pushing local tax hard due to government funding shortfall.
findings.quote: The MTFP assumes the Council will increase Band D Council Tax to the maximum level permitted without triggering a referendum. These increases over the period have the potential to generate an additional annual income of £1.995 million by 2030/31.

findings.paper_title: MTFP - Scene Setting - General Fund report and Appendices 1-5
findings.headline: Fees and charges strategy has delivered £2.5 million additional income over three years, exceeding 20% target; car parking and Keyhaven charges increased from 1 January 2027
findings.detail: Council achieved approximately £2.5m additional fees and charges income over 2024/25–2026/27, surpassing the 20% growth target (equivalent to 6.3% annualised). From 1 January 2027, car parking fees increased generating estimated £189k additional annual income; Keyhaven river fees increased generating £7k. For 2027/28 onwards, policy shifts to use CPI as guideline for annual uplifts unless alternative approach justified by market conditions.
findings.matters: Demonstrates fees and charges as reliable and effective income lever; shows council has successfully extracted growth and has potential for further increases; provides benchmark for peer councils on achievable growth rates; is part of strategy to offset structural deficit.
findings.figures: £2.5m additional income over 3 years (2024/25–2026/27); car parking additional income £189k from 1 January 2027; Keyhaven additional income £7k from 1 January 2027; fees and charges growth target £300k for 2027/28
findings.quote: During this three year period the Council generated approximately £2.5 million of additional gross fees and charges income, thereby surpassing its 20% target.

findings.paper_title: MTFP - Scene Setting - General Fund report and Appendices 1-5
findings.headline: Waste service budget impacts still being resolved with resource adjustments pending completion of review of new service model
findings.detail: New waste service has been fully rolled out district-wide following significant one-off investment (temporary staff, bin acquisition, delivery, advisory support). A full operational review is now underway. Report states that 'full clarity on the budget requirements for future years is still being established and resources may need to be adjusted once the review has concluded and the new ways of working are fully defined'.
findings.matters: Creates contingent adjustment risk to MTFP forecasts; budget assumptions will change once review concludes; illustrates timing lag between service transformation and financial stabilization; review could reveal operational pressures requiring additional investment or conversely identify efficiencies.
findings.figures: No quantum specified for future adjustments; current budget impact of £54k reduction in 2027/28 (net of various one-off items)
findings.quote: A full review of the new waste service is being conducted now that a consistent district wide service is being provided. Any adjustments to budgets will need to be included in future updates.

findings.paper_title: MTFP - Scene Setting - General Fund report and Appendices 1-5
findings.headline: Investment income budget cut by £250,000 in each of 2027/28 and 2028/29 as interest rates fall and cash drawdown increases
findings.detail: Council reduced investment income budget by £250k for both 2027/28 and 2028/29 despite achieving investment income better than budget in recent years. Reduction reflects acknowledgment of 'downward trend' in interest rates and 'increased requirement to utilise cash balances'. Bank of England base rate has fallen from 5.25% peak in 2023/24 to 3.75% currently.
findings.matters: Interest rate advantage councils briefly enjoyed is reversing; treasury income will continue to decline; removes a small source of positive variance that has helped balance budgets in recent years; forecasts higher cash burn rate.
findings.figures: Investment income reduction £250k in each of 2027/28 and 2028/29; base rate 3.75% (down from 5.25% peak)
findings.quote: in recognition of the downward trend and the increased requirement to utilise cash balances, the investment income budget has been reduced by £250,000 in both 2027/28 and 2028/29.

findings.paper_title: MTFP - Scene Setting - General Fund report and Appendices 1-5
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation additional resource requirements continuing to be quantified with £1.850 million reserve held but sufficiency uncertain
findings.detail: Following the recent pause to the LGR programme, the council is seeking cost recovery for amounts already spent on transition planning. However, 'additional resources are still likely to be required to support a safe and legally compliant transition'. Work is ongoing to quantify the required capacity across all council functions and determine whether existing budget provision and the £1.850m LGR reserve will be sufficient. Creates material uncertainty over future costs and reserve adequacy.
findings.matters: Material going concern uncertainty; LGR timeline is unconfirmed; additional transition costs may emerge; reserve of £1.850m may prove insufficient; affects medium-term financial sustainability and planning assumptions.
findings.figures: Devolution and Local Government Reorganisation Reserve £1.850m
findings.quote: Work is continuing to quantify the level of additional capacity required across all Council functions and to determine whether the existing budget provision and Devolution and Local Government Reorganisation Reserve are sufficient to meet these requirements.
